newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end in retreat, down over one pct.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end in retreat, down over one pct.

text.p: French shares ended down more than one percent, taking their lead from a lower Wall Street to consolidate last week's substantial gains, traders said.

The market, which traded in negative ground all day, earlier tumbled after bond markets took fright on comments from the Bundesbank's chief economist Otmar Issing that there was no reason for further cuts in key interest rates.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 26.75 points or 1.23 percent at 2,148.86, while the CAC-40 futures contract was down seven at 2,152 from Tuesday's settle.
* Volume was brisk six billion francs
* Eridania Beghin-Say jumped 1.77 percent to 803 francs on prospects of cheaper raw materials.
The stock also benefited from a Saint-Louis presentation to analysts this morning which pointed to promising prospects for the food ingredients sector
* Gan ends off lows, down 0.82 percent at 120.50, after reporting first-half net loss of nearly one billion francs
* Club Med dives 17.34 percent to 329 francs after Tuesday's profit warning. The share fall prompts Paribas to put a sell note on hotelier Accor.
* Cheuvreux de Virieu took Club Med off its recommended list, while SGE Delahaye dropped it to underperform from outperform.
* Industry minister Franck Borotra told the National Assembly that there have not been any offers for the Thomson group other than those from Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom.
French newspapers have reported a French businessman was lining up a bid to keep Thomson Multimedia under French control
* Lagardere drops 6.24 percent to 166.70 after last week's run up on prospects for buying Thomson.
* Credit National shares tumbled 3.67 percent to 236 francs after another newspaper report focusing on a risk of downgrades by rating agencies.
* Prime Minister Alain Juppe appearing on 1730 GMT main evening news programme on France 3.
